QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_22

question.text: Under the SEBI circular on Investor Charter for AIFs, how must the Investor Charter be published for a NEW AIF scheme?

answer.text: It should be disclosed to investors on their registered e-mail ID as a one-time measure.
It should be disclosed in the PPM of the new scheme.
It should be uploaded on the AMFI website within 30 days of scheme launch.
It should be filed separately with SEBI prior to launch, outside the PPM.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the December 10, 2021 SEBI circular on Investor Charter: for NEW schemes, the Investor Charter must be disclosed in the PPM. For EXISTING schemes, it had to be disclosed to investors on their registered e-mail ID as a one-time measure. AMFI is unrelated (mutual-fund body). The Trap: The e-mail disclosure mechanism applies to EXISTING schemes, not new ones. AMFI is not the regulator-level publication channel for AIFs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same Investor Charter rollout. The Charter's contents overlap with but are distinct from PPM Section X (Risk Factors) — do not substitute one for the other. Manager's Pro-Tip: Embed the Investor Charter as a standalone annexure to every new PPM. LPs routinely cross-check the Charter against actual fund practice during complaints; inconsistency is a fast route to a SCORES reference.
